Identified by the monument, which stands in front of the Gabaldon building, and by the L-shaped Gabaldon plan; satellite imagery inspected October 9, 2026. Edit dates are not construction dates. The school grounds stay the separate Naga Central School I and II landmarks.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Gabaldon School Buildings
sources.note: Act No. 1801 (1907), the prototype plans by William E. Parsons in straight, L- and U-shaped forms, and Republic Act No. 11194 (2019).

text.en: Gabaldon schoolhouses take their name from the 1907 Gabaldon Law, Act No. 1801; their prototype plans, by William E. Parsons, came in straight, L- and U-shaped forms.
The school's Parents-Teachers Association erected a monument to José María Panganiban in front of the building in 1930.
Long unmarked and nearly demolished, the monument was identified as Panganiban's in 2013, during a city inspection of the heritage building.
The Gabaldon building was listed for preservation by City Ordinance No. 2003-003.
